answer: An agent economy can anchor each identity to one wildflower meadow plot stewarded under an independent conservation trust. The steward must tend it through a full season, and the warden inspects it at unannounced visits timed to the sun's zenith, logging bloom and soil work no script fakes. Each plot builds one bridge corridor, and the trust issues only one plot per person, so a farm cannot buy plots in bulk. The stewardship fee in outside money doubles per further plot on the same funding trail, so each extra fake costs another real meadow, another season of labor, and twice the prior fee.
